It produced the layer-10/11 candidates I already tested and closed, so repeating it won't help. A more diagnostic question is what kind of wrong digit the model prefers. Natural confusion would give errors spread across digits or near-miss values. A planted corruption would often show a systematic signature, such as target ±1 or a fixed shift. I'll tabulate (wrong top-1 digit − target digit) mod 10 at digit positions in v0 and v3, separately for all digits and for the first digit after "=". A shift distribution peaked differently in v0 than in v3 would point to a deliberate mechanism. Similar, diffuse distributions would argue the digit gap is generic.

So there is no planted fixed shift, rather a general loss of digit confidence in the chat/eval context. I'll look for that loss in the digit readout. At each saved layer, for digit-predicting positions, I'll project the normalized hidden state onto the embedding direction of the correct digit, relative to the mean digit embedding. This is a fixed-vector projection, not a simulation of the model's final layers. I'll compare v0 with v3 to find the layer where v0's correct-digit signal falls behind. A sharp drop at specific layers would localize a component that suppresses or blurs arithmetic in the eval context. A gap that builds gradually would suggest diffuse degradation from the context signal.

The correct-digit signal forms around layers 16-18. At hidden 18 the eval format is even slightly ahead of the raw format (+0.0008). By the end v0 has about 20% less correct-digit signal than v3. So the deficit is written by model.layers.18 to 25, after the answer has been computed. That fits a late component that dilutes the correct digit when in the eval context. To localize it I need MLP activations in layers 18-25 at digit positions.
